definition: The material element of language that represents the subject for another signifier in the symbolic order

contrasts.differential: The signifier is the material form, the signified is the meaning effect that slides beneath it

definition: The meaning effect produced by the play of signifiers, always sliding beneath the signifying chain

contrasts.differential: The signified is meaning, the signifier is material form; the signified is an effect of signifier chain

definition: That which resists symbolization absolutely, the impossible kernel that escapes the symbolic and imaginary

contrasts.differential: The Real is what cannot be symbolized, the Symbolic is the order of language and law
The Real shatters imaginary wholeness, the Imaginary is the domain of images and identification

definition: The order of language, law, and social structure that constitutes the subject through signification

contrasts.differential: The Symbolic operates through differential signifiers, the Imaginary through images and resemblance
The Symbolic structures reality through language, the Real is what escapes this structuring

definition: The order of images, identifications, and the dual relation, founded on the mirror stage

contrasts.differential: The Imaginary is based on resemblance and wholeness, the Symbolic on difference and lack
The Imaginary provides illusory completeness, the Real exposes its impossibility

definition: The object-cause of desire, the remainder that falls out of the symbolic order and drives desire

contrasts.differential: objet a is the lost object-cause, the Other is the locus of speech and the signifying chain

definition: The locus of the signifier, language, and the law; the place from which the subject receives its message

contrasts.differential: The Other is the symbolic locus, objet a is what falls out of it as remainder

definition: Enjoyment beyond the pleasure principle, a painful excessive satisfaction that transgresses limits

contrasts.differential: jouissance is excessive satisfaction beyond limits, desire is constituted by lack and sustained by prohibition
jouissance transgresses the pleasure principle, pleasure operates within homeostatic limits

definition: The metonymy of lack, always directed beyond any particular object, constituted by the desire of the Other

contrasts.differential: Desire is symbolic and cannot be satisfied, need is biological and can be met
Desire is the remainder when need is articulated as demand
Desire sustains itself through lack, jouissance aims at its abolition

definition: The articulation of need in language, which always exceeds need by carrying a demand for love

contrasts.differential: Demand is need articulated in language plus demand for love, need is biological
Demand can be satisfied, desire is the unsatisfiable remainder between demand and need

definition: The fundamental signifier that anchors the symbolic order and institutes the law of prohibition

contrasts.differential: The Name-of-the-Father structures neurosis, its foreclosure produces psychosis

definition: The primordial rejection of a signifier from the symbolic, specifically the Name-of-the-Father in psychosis

contrasts.differential: Foreclosure rejects from the symbolic entirely, repression keeps within the symbolic as unconscious
Foreclosure of the Name-of-the-Father is the mechanism of psychosis

definition: The mechanism by which signifiers are rendered unconscious while remaining within the symbolic order

contrasts.differential: Repression keeps the signifier in the symbolic unconscious, foreclosure expels it entirely

definition: Substitution of one signifier for another, producing a new signification; the mechanism of symptoms

contrasts.differential: Metaphor is substitution producing new meaning, metonymy is displacement along the signifying chain

definition: Displacement along the signifying chain, the endless sliding of signification; the mechanism of desire

contrasts.differential: Metonymy is horizontal displacement, metaphor is vertical substitution

definition: The formative moment when the infant identifies with its image, founding the ego as imaginary alienation
The operation by which the subject is articulated to the signifying chain as the element that is lacking
The divided subject constituted by the signifier, barred from full self-knowledge by the unconscious

contrasts.differential: The subject is the effect of the signifier, the ego is an imaginary construction

definition: The imaginary construction formed through identification with the mirror image, a locus of méconnaissance

contrasts.differential: The ego is imaginary misrecognition, the subject is the effect of symbolic division

definition: A metaphorical formation of the unconscious where a repressed signifier returns in disguised form

contrasts.differential: The symptom is to be interpreted, the sinthome is what holds the subject's structure together

definition: The fourth ring that ties together the Real, Symbolic, and Imaginary, a singular mode of jouissance

contrasts.differential: The sinthome is structural and not to be dissolved, the symptom is a message to be deciphered

definition: A constant force that circles around the object without ever reaching it, distinct from biological instinct

contrasts.differential: The drive circles around its object, desire is sustained by lack of the object
The drive has no natural object, instinct has a biological aim and object
